request.description: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment.

things: The Technical Group reports a small concern local to its tec (to country_one)
The Legal Group reports a small concern local to its legal a (to country_two)
The Logistics Group reports a small concern local to its log (to country_three)
The Community Group reports a small concern local to its com (to country_four)
Regular meeting of the partnership members.
Deadline for the partnership's activation decision.
a new work cycle every 4 rounds

review_findings.description_words: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system.
review_findings.problem: No mechanic or process allows the partnership or its members to actually decide on, approve, delay, or block the activation of the early-warning system, nor does anything check or change member.authorized or member.approved when the activation-deadline arrives.

review_findings.description_words: Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members.
review_findings.problem: All four information and delivery entities start with active=true and status="delivered" while the recipient members start with aware=false, so coordination.action.communicate is impossible from the start and cannot be used to deliver any concerns.

review_findings.description_words: Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members.
review_findings.problem: The raise-local-concern mechanic only flips a boolean flag on the acting group itself and does not transmit the concern through a channel to a partnership member or link to any member's ability to reopen issues or make support conditional.

review_findings.description_words: Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment.
review_findings.problem: Although a regular-member-meeting moment ticks in the background, no mechanic references it, slows meetings down when concerns are raised, or allows conditional support and reopened issues to delay or block deployment.

When activation-deadline reaches ticks_until = 0, moment-occurs sets ticks_until to every_ticks (-1), causing the deadline to pass silently with no effect on the decision or the ability to continue acting after the deadline.

actors.explanation: Partnership sees only public institutional state, member roles, and public positions without any private concerns or unauthorized disclosures.

Country One's visible state for info-technical-local-concern-to-country-one asserts as fact that "A small, true technical concern local to the technical group's area has been raised", which improperly reveals to the recipient that the concern is objectively true rather than merely a claim they were exposed to.

Country Two's visible state for info-legal-local-concern-to-country-two asserts as fact that "A small, true legal concern local to the legal group's area has been raised", which improperly reveals to the recipient that the concern is objectively true rather than merely a claim they were exposed to.

Country Three's visible state for info-logistics-local-concern-to-country-three asserts as fact that "A small, true logistics concern local to the logistics group's area has been raised", which improperly reveals to the recipient that the concern is objectively true rather than merely a claim they were exposed to.

Country Four's visible state for info-community-local-concern-to-country-four asserts as fact that "A small, true community concern local to the community group's area has been raised", which improperly reveals to the recipient that the concern is objectively true rather than merely a claim they were exposed to.
Regional Health Network sees only shared institutional state, public member roles, and public positions without any private concerns or unauthorized disclosures.

Technical Group sees public institutional state and its own local technical concern and channel delivery to Country One, matching the description that it raises a small, true local concern through its own channel.

Legal Group sees public institutional state and its own local legal concern and channel delivery to Country Two, matching the description that it raises a small, true local concern through its own channel.

Logistics Group sees public institutional state and its own local logistics concern and channel delivery to Country Three, matching the description that it raises a small, true local concern through its own channel.

Community Group sees public institutional state and its own local community concern and channel delivery to Country Four, matching the description that it raises a small, true local concern through its own channel.

canonical_state_review.explanation: Current material facts are canonically owned without conflicting duplicates: technical_condition.passing on condition-activate-early-warning-system owns current technical truth (updated only by decision.action.repair-condition); validation_decision on activate-early-warning-system owns validation, hold, review, assents, and active status (updated by request-review, complete-validation, validation-passes, validation-fails, record-assent, withdraw-assent, and activate); and each actor_position entity owns that actor's stance and assent. The information entities represent static initial concern claims rather than duplicate current technical condition or decision state.

fidelity_assumptions: The four unnamed countries are represented with neutral labels; no country-specific characteristics are inferred.
The four concerns are represented only by their stated domains and local scope; their specific contents are not invented.

Each concern is initially delivered to a different country: technical to Country One, legal to Country Two, logistics to Country Three, and community to Country Four. This mapping is an explicit modeling assumption because the scenario does not identify recipients.
The regional health network is treated as a member whose support counts in the activation decision.
A regular meeting every three ticks and a deadline at tick 12 are illustrative scheduling choices, not scenario-specified dates.
The technical condition is assumed initially passing, with validation untested. The scenario does not specify a technical failure; reports alone do not change the actual condition.
All five members are required for activation in this representation; the scenario does not specify a quorum or voting threshold.
unsupported: The schema does not specify particular contents, evidence, or impacts for the local concerns beyond their domains and truth within local scope.

The schema does not provide detailed meeting procedures for slowing an agenda, reopening settled issues, or making support conditional; these remain possible behaviors rather than scripted transitions.
The scenario does not specify a voting threshold, formal authority, or deadline consequence such as automatic rejection or postponement.
The scenario does not specify a technical repair or validation protocol, so no repairer or technical fix is asserted.
unresolved_questions: What are the specific local concerns and what evidence supports them?
Which member receives each concern, and does the regional health network receive any directly?
What support threshold and formal decision procedure govern activation?
What is the deadline date, and what happens if no decision is reached by then?
Who is authorized to validate or repair the system, and what tests establish that it is ready?

review_findings.description_words: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system.
review_findings.problem: No mechanic or process allows the partnership or its members to actually decide on, approve, delay, or block the activation of the early-warning system, nor does anything check or change member.authorized or member.approved when the activation-deadline arrives.

review_findings.description_words: Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members.
review_findings.problem: All four information and delivery entities start with active=true and status="delivered" while the recipient members start with aware=false, so coordination.action.communicate is impossible from the start and cannot be used to deliver any concerns.

review_findings.description_words: Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members.
review_findings.problem: The raise-local-concern mechanic only flips a boolean flag on the acting group itself and does not transmit the concern through a channel to a partnership member or link to any member's ability to reopen issues or make support conditional.

review_findings.description_words: Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment.
review_findings.problem: Although a regular-member-meeting moment ticks in the background, no mechanic references it, slows meetings down when concerns are raised, or allows conditional support and reopened issues to delay or block deployment.

When activation-deadline reaches ticks_until = 0, moment-occurs sets ticks_until to every_ticks (-1), causing the deadline to pass silently with no effect on the decision or the ability to continue acting after the deadline.

not_modeled: The specific content and practical remedy for each local concern are not specified.
The scenario does not specify which member supports activation, the conditions attached to support, the required support threshold, or the exact decision procedure.
No technical validation, repair authority, or technical activation condition is specified.
The scenario does not specify the exact deadline date or the frequency of regular meetings.

regular-member-meeting.label: Regular meeting of the partnership members.

activation_question.question: Whether to activate the cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system.

judge.ruling: The partnership may convene the represented regular member meeting, making it happen now. The installed processes do not cover an early convening, so this needs a new rule; it does not itself decide the activation question.
judge.reasoning: Convening changes the represented meeting’s state, and no installed move covers that change. The schedule-based process does not block convening early, but only handles occurrence at its scheduled countdown.
facts: Actor is partnership, with categories actor and member; its member.role is “Partnership of four countries and a regional health network deciding whether to activate the system.”
The named meeting is regular-member-meeting, with categories moment and regular-member-meeting; moment.happening_now is false and moment.ticks_until is 1.
The partnership description says it convenes regular member meetings.
blockers: No installed action or mechanic covers convening a meeting or changing the meeting’s moment.happening_now state.

The installed moment-occurs process only makes the meeting happen when ticks_until is 0; at present it is 1. The existing vote mechanic requires a meeting to be happening, but does not provide a way to convene one.
judge.why: The test run accepted the partnership’s convene-regular-member-meeting move and set the regular meeting’s happening_now value from false to true, with no blockers. That matches the ruling’s intended effect.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in

decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.

messages.content:
You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.

messages.content:
You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.

messages.content:
You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

messages.content:
You are an actor in a represented simulated world.

Each turn you say what you physically try to do: anything a person in
your place could try with their body, voice or hands, or wait. You do
not decide whether it works or what it causes. The world's own rules
decide that afterwards, and you find out from what you see next. Do not
describe outcomes, only what you try.

You are shown some things you know you can do here. You may do one of
them, or try something else; something you are not shown may simply
not work.

Act coherently from the current visible situation, the world's stated
purpose and, when you are given one, who you are. Act as that person
would from their own goals, beliefs and tendencies, not as a helper
steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold
back, attach conditions to their support or wait; someone who disagrees
may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

An offered action may include an `[effects: ...]` annotation. That is a
preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

An information item's `content` is what it said when it was first sent
and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.

rulings.description: Tell one other partnership member the actor's stated position on activation during a regular member meeting.
rulings.ruling: A member can tell one other member its position during a meeting; that changes the recipient's represented awareness. No other member's agreement is needed. This single-recipient move cannot represent telling all four named members in one action; it can be used separately for each. The proposed move requires the meeting to be happening, so the attempt as currently timed is blocked.
rulings.why: The test run correctly refuses the move because the regular meeting is not happening now (actual false, required true). That matches the meeting precondition; the current state does not permit telling members at the meeting yet.

action.description: Tell one other partnership member the actor's stated position on activation during a regular member meeting.

mechanic.rationale: A member may communicate its stated position to one other member at a happening regular meeting; the represented effect is that the recipient becomes aware, not that the recipient agrees.

statement: A nonempty statement must be supplied.

checks.label: The recipient is not the actor
The actor belongs to the partnership
The recipient belongs to the partnership

limits: This move records awareness only; it does not record agreement or change the recipient's vote.
One move has one recipient; telling multiple members requires separate moves.
tests: A partnership member can tell one other member a nonempty position statement during a happening regular member meeting; the recipient becomes aware.
The move is refused if the meeting is not happening, the recipient is the actor, either person is not a partnership member, or the statement is empty.
semantic_bindings: recipient is the member being told
meeting is the represented regular member meeting
statement is the actor's supplied position text

describe outcomes, only what you try.

steering the world toward a good outcome: a cautious person may hold

may object or obstruct. Avoid pointless repetition when another
available action is clearly more useful to you.

preview derived from the installed world mechanic that will execute the
action. Treat it as authoritative for what the action changes. Do not
assume or describe additional effects that are absent from that preview.

and never changes. When the item also carries a `concern` record, that
record's `status` is where the concern stands now: `resolved` means its
remedy has been carried out and what the content describes has been
dealt with, until someone reopens it or a review finds it again.

rulings.description: Tell one other partnership member the actor's stated position on activation during a regular member meeting.
rulings.ruling: A member can tell one other member its position during a meeting; that changes the recipient's represented awareness. No other member's agreement is needed. This single-recipient move cannot represent telling all four named members in one action; it can be used separately for each. The proposed move requires the meeting to be happening, so the attempt as currently timed is blocked.
rulings.why: The test run correctly refuses the move because the regular meeting is not happening now (actual false, required true). That matches the meeting precondition; the current state does not permit telling members at the meeting yet.

rulings.ruling: A member can tell one other member its position during a meeting; that changes the recipient's represented awareness. No other member's agreement is needed. This single-recipient move cannot represent telling all four named members in one action; it can be used separately for each. The proposed move requires the meeting to be happening, so the attempt as currently timed is blocked.
rulings.why: The test run correctly refuses the move because the regular meeting is not happening now (actual false, required true). That matches the meeting precondition; the current state does not permit telling members at the meeting yet.

rulings.description: Tell one other partnership member the actor's stated position on activation during a regular member meeting.
rulings.ruling: A member can tell one other member its position during a meeting; that changes the recipient's represented awareness. No other member's agreement is needed. This single-recipient move cannot represent telling all four named members in one action; it can be used separately for each. The proposed move requires the meeting to be happening, so the attempt as currently timed is blocked.
rulings.why: The test run correctly refuses the move because the regular meeting is not happening now (actual false, required true). That matches the meeting precondition; the current state does not permit telling members at the meeting yet.
